overview: This Senate resolution supports naming October 4 to October 10, 2026, "National 4-H Week." 4-H is the country's largest youth development organization, serving nearly 6 million young people through hands-on projects in science, health, agriculture and civic engagement. It is run through the Cooperative Extension System, a network of more than 110 land-grant universities, with the Agriculture Department's National Institute of Food and Agriculture as its federal partner. The resolution recognizes 4-H's role in building leadership skills and thanks its roughly 500,000 volunteers and 3,500 professionals. The Senate approved it by unanimous consent on September 29, 2026.
for: Supporters say 4-H has a long record of teaching young people practical skills and leadership, and the week highlights that work in communities nationwide.
against: Critics say the resolution is symbolic: it does not change any law or provide new funding for 4-H or extension programs.
